document.executive_summary: Facilities Engineering must select one HVAC control package on measured energy alone. Recomputing from the trusted WO-02 table, all four candidates clear both gates: quality P4 100, P3 98, P1 92, P2 82 against the 80 floor, and defects P2 1, P3 2, P1 3, P4 5 against the 5 ceiling. Energy on the shared duty basis is P4 9, P3 20, P2 33 and P1 50 kWh, giving gaps of +11, +24 and +41 kWh above the minimum; these match analyst A's figures exactly. P4 is therefore the lowest-energy qualifying package, and my independent ballot is P4. Residual questions are recorded, not resolved.

recommendation.rationale: P4 qualifies with quality 100 and defects 5, exactly at the ceiling, and posts the lowest measured energy, 9 kWh, 11 kWh below runner-up P3, on the shared duty basis. The ceiling-level defect count is an audit contingency, not an override; if a regrade disqualifies P4, the same table facts make P3 the fallback at 20 kWh.

sections.body: The screen has two independent gates. Quality runs P4 100, P3 98, P1 92 and P2 82; every value clears the 80 floor, and P2's +2 is the smallest margin, so a single regrade could push it below the floor. Defects run P2 1, P3 2, P1 3 and P4 5; every count is inside the ceiling, and P4 sits exactly on it, so one added defect would disqualify the current leader. No candidate is eliminated; eligibility is settled from the trusted table alone, with no additional sources required.
